clue.text: Freezing bend leads to nervous movement

parts.note: an arc is a curve or bend
a tic is an involuntary twitch of the nerves

explanation.surface: A doctor describing how a cold-induced cramp brings on a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic conditions are bitterly cold, so the adjective is a synonym for freezing.

clue.text: One of The Simpsons in broadcast knocked back wine

indicators.note: the footballer's initials sit inside the other piece
knocked back says the word for broadcast is turned round, as a drink is knocked back

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
O.J. Simpson, the American footballer, is jokingly one of the Simpsons

explanation.surface: A cartoon character on TV gulping down a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The cartoon family is a red herring: the Simpson is the footballer O.J., and 'knocked back' turns only the broadcast word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish wine from the region of that name.

clue.text: Check French game virtually hot, making Mediterranean dish

parts.note: to keep tabs on something is to check it, so a tab is a check

indicators.note: virtually means almost entirely, so the game's name loses its last letter

parts.note: boules is the French bowling game played on gravel
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A holiday scene: checking on a French bowls match in the heat before cooking a Mediterranean meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virtually' drops the final S of BOULES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabbouleh is a Levantine salad of bulgur wheat, parsley and mint, eaten around the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: I'll be blowed given score?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'I'll be blowed'
to net is to score a goal, so net stands for score

explanation.surface: A cry of astonishment at being told the result.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes a brass instrument: it is blown, given a musical score to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornet is a small brass instrument that a player blows while reading from a score.

clue.text: Current agents pursuing free bread

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the agents and current come after the word for free

parts.note: FOC stands for free of charge
AC is alternating current
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, its staff agents

explanation.surface: Electricity workers chasing after a free loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Focaccia is a flat Italian bread, often topped with olive oil and herbs.

clue.text: Financial backers lifting business? That is evident in enclosure after match

indicators.note: after says the rest comes behind the word for match

parts.note: a friendly is a match played for no competitive stake

indicators.note: evident in says the business and that-is pieces are seen inside the enclosure

parts.note: a sty is a pen or enclosure for pigs

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue raises the abbreviation, reading it upwards

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
IE is id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Sponsors buying a company, spotted in a hospitality box after the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting' reads the business abbreviation upwards, as OC, in this down entry; a friendly is a non-competitive match.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly society is a British mutual association that pays out benefits to members, so its members back one another financially.

clue.text: Bearing first of children months out of wedlock

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word for offspring
out of says the abbreviation for months leaves the word for wedlock

parts.note: wedlock is the state of marriage

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about having a child months before the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of wedlock' looks like a phrase about illegitimacy, but 'out of' removes M from MARRIAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means the way one holds oneself, one's posture or deportment, as does bearing.

clue.text: Jerseys perhaps picked up in sailing centre

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for the cattle is taken by its sound

parts.note: Jerseys are a breed of dairy cattle, so cows by example

explanation.surface: Woollen jumpers, perhaps, bought at a yachting town.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerseys look like sweaters but are cattle. Cowes is on the Isle of Wight, home of Cowes Week regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowes is the British yachting town that hosts the famous annual sailing regatta.

clue.text: Vastness of the author's toilet I tardily vacated

parts.note: the author's means the author is, I'M, the setter speaking
the mens is a gents' toilet

indicators.note: vacated empties the word of its insides, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A writer describing how slowly they left a huge lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Immensity is enormous size or extent, the quality of being vast.

clue.text: Airman's heading off stronger after personal problem seen by doctor

indicators.note: after places the stronger word behind the problem and doctor

parts.note: BO is body odour, a personal hygiene problem
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word for stronger

parts.note: hardier means tougher or stronger

explanation.surface: A pilot visits the doctor about an embarrassing problem and leaves stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airman's' is 'airman is', the definition and link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is the aircrew member who aims and releases the bombs, so an airman.

clue.text: Mammal not at place of origin

indicators.note: not says the following two letters are absent from the mammal

parts.note: a wombat is an Australian marsupial mammal

explanation.surface: A zoologist noting an animal missing from its birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The uterus is where every mammal begins life, its first home before birth.

clue.text: Nick grabs a lead from room, getting approving cry of King Charles

indicators.note: grabs says the prison word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: nick and can are both slang for prison

indicators.note: lead from takes the first letter of the word room

parts.note: ole is the Spanish shout of approval

explanation.surface: A policeman arrests someone in a room, to the cheers of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is a noun for jail here, not a verb for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolean describes the reign or period of Charles I or Charles II, from Latin Carolus.

clue.text: Shandy drained during pub crawl, primarily harmonious

indicators.note: during puts the drained drink inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: drained empties the drink of its middle letters, keeping only the outer ones
primarily picks the first letter of crawl

explanation.surface: Friends on a pub crawl, harmoniously finishing their shandies.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in sync means moving in step, perfectly matched or in agreement.

clue.text: Revolutionary Liberal shot in the arm and face

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a shot in the arm is a boost, aid

explanation.surface: A radical politician wounded in the arm and the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot in the arm' looks like a wound, but means help: AID.
explanation.definitionFit: The dial is the face of a clock or watch, marked with numbers.

clue.text: Among other things, domestic forgets back of television and divan regularly

indicators.note: forgets says a letter is left out of the word for domestic

parts.note: domestic as in internal affairs, home not foreign

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of television
regularly takes every other letter of divan

explanation.surface: A household inventory: a TV set and a divan, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgets back of television' drops N from INTERNAL; divan's even letters give IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for among other things.

clue.text: A girl poshly spoken returned and deposited money for cases

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl
laid means put down or deposited

explanation.surface: A well-to-do young woman came back and paid money into her account.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use a posh 'gel' is a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is state funding for people who cannot afford lawyers in court cases.

clue.text: Girl nails routine that's performed near curtains?

indicators.note: nails means pins in place, so the girl holds the routine word inside

parts.note: lass is a girl
trite means routine, hackneyed

explanation.surface: A girl perfectly executes a stage routine just before the curtain falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' is slang for death, not a theatre's drapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The last rites are sacraments a priest gives to a person about to die, near the end.

clue.text: Anxious time to abandon cricket perhaps, before game turns against England

indicators.note: before puts the insect remainder ahead of the game piece
against means placed next to, beside England's letter
to abandon says the abbreviation for time leaves the insect word

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect

indicators.note: turns means the game's letters are reversed

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A nervous player about to give up cricket for rugby, which turns against England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket perhaps' is the insect, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means unsure of oneself, worried, uneasy.

clue.text: Mate briefly probing gets to rearrange pieces of art?

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so the mate goes inside
to rearrange tells us to shuffle the letters of gets

parts.note: china (plate) is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, cut short here

explanation.surface: A friend poking around and moving bits of artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To rearrange' makes ETGS. China plate means mate in Cockney rhyming slang, and 'briefly' clips its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from acid-cut metal plates, works of art.

clue.text: First year's swelling

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, the first two words having the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A first-year student has a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: There is barely an indicator: 'year's' read as 'year has' holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small inflamed swelling on the eyelid.

clue.text: Notice a period of sleep on chest

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the sleep piece above the chest

parts.note: REM, rapid eye movement, is a phase of sleep
an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Spotting someone napping on top of a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to notice or observe, and to say so.

clue.text: Father left leaving fruit drink

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: leaving says the abbreviation for left exits the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A priest walks off leaving a juice drink behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A frappe is an iced drink, often blended coffee or liqueur over crushed ice.

clue.text: Cap'n and I going off course in this?

definitions.text: Cap'n and I going off course in this?

indicators.note: going off course says the captain and I letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor worries what he and his captain will feel if the ship strays.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is the sudden fear that grips sailors when their vessel goes astray.

clue.text: Musical character, holding discussions, about to make tracks

indicators.note: holding means the musical sign contains the other piece

parts.note: a clef is a symbol written at the start of a musical stave

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for discussions is reversed

parts.note: fora is a plural of forum, meetings for discussion

explanation.surface: A stage-show figure in talks before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical character' suggests a role in a show; it is a written symbol. 'About' turns FORA into AROF.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear off is to leave quickly, as does to make tracks.

clue.text: American actor one day finishes off partnering female

indicators.note: partnering means joined alongside the abbreviation for female
finishes off removes the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star who one day ends up with a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' trims both 'one' and 'day' to ON and DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry, Jane and Peter Fonda are all well-known Hollywood film stars.

clue.text: With finals coming in nursing school, Nancy's in depression

indicators.note: finals means the final letters of the two words

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, and there in is en

explanation.surface: A nursing student called Nancy falling into depression at exam time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finals' suggests exams; it takes the last letters. Nancy is a French city, so its word for in is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, a depression in the land, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: It's easy to cut back investing in ointment, having spent over grand

indicators.note: investing in means going into, so the reversed cut word sits inside
having spent means used up, so the cricket abbreviation for over is gone

parts.note: unction is an ointment, as used for anointing
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: back says the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to axe is to cut
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Easy, says someone dipping into a pot of ointment after splashing out a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns AXE into EXA, inserted in UNCTIN (UNCTION losing O). 'It's' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undemanding asks little of you, so it is easy.

clue.text: Heading off, ex-PM visits end of armoury where origins of pike displayed?

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the former prime minister

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was a British prime minister

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of armoury

explanation.surface: A former PM visiting an arsenal where spears are on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pike suggests weapons with the armoury, but it is a fish: its origins are eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchery is where fish such as pike are bred from eggs and hatched.

clue.text: African stronghold for soul party with moving music at heart

indicators.note: moving says one letter is shifted to a new place

parts.note: ka is the ancient Egyptian spirit or soul
a bash is a party

indicators.note: at heart picks the central letter of the word music

explanation.surface: A soul music party with dancing, a picture of a lively night out.
explanation.walkthrough: The S in BASH, which is the middle of 'music', moves two places left.
explanation.definitionFit: A kasbah is the citadel of a North African city, a fortress.
